title: GT17-670GD - EVOLVED OPERATIONAL USER INTERFACES (EXPRO+)
description: Existing operational user interfaces for ground segment are primarily built on aging software platforms characterized by deprecated technologies, a monolithic architecture and rigid implementation. While these legacy platforms provide stability for established scenarios, it struggles to adapt to modern operational demands specifically the introduction of remote operations, cloud infrastructure management, and the seamless integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI). Building on the EGS-CC WebUI and the PulseUI, a specialized WebUI branch tailored for operational environments, the new approach has enabled support for comprehensive UI testing, facilitate remote control capabilities, and better align with the microservices architecture backends. To overcome these challenges and achieve the goals of the project, an architectural and design approach based on the following will be required: - Web-Based Architecture: To guarantee high flexibility and stability. - Unified Design System: Establishing a common look and feel across the ground segment.  - Industry-Standard Framework Principles: Adopting the principles of established UI frameworks (such as Material Design). This will provide a comprehensive suite of reusable components, complete with intuitive documentation and tutorials, hence mitigates the risk of "technology islands".

title: UA_AD02 DESIGN, DEVELOPMENT, AND TESTING OF A MEMBRANELESS ELECTROLYZER FOR ENERGY AND LIFE-SUPPORT SYSTEMS AND ISRU TECHNOLOGIES - EXPRO PLUS
description: The availability of oxygen and hydrogen is a key enabling capability for future lunar exploration architectures. These products areexpected to support energy systems, environmental control and life-support systems, and In-Situ Resource Utilisation (ISRU) activities. In the longer term, future exploration missions are expected to increasingly rely on indigenous resources to improve sustainability and reduce logistics requirements. The capability to produce oxygen and hydrogen from locally available resources is therefore considered a strategic enabling technology. The objective of this activity is to design, develop and test a membraneless electrolysertechnology suitable for future space exploration applications, with particular emphasis on the production of oxygen and hydrogen using feedstocks representative of future lunar ISRU scenarios.

title: ASSESSMENT OF LASER COMMUNICATION TERMINAL FOR VERY-LOW EARTH ORBIT SATELLITES (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 5H.014) - EXPRO+
description: Objective: The objective of this study is to assess market needs and the delta developments required to adapt current LEO optical communication terminals designsfor use at Very-Low Earth Orbits (VLEO).TargetedImprovements:To enable laser communications from VLEO platforms.Description: Very-Low Earth Orbit (VLEO) orbit is particularly advantageous for satellite communication due to its proximity to the Earth's surface, resulting in reducedlatency, stronger signal and improved link budgets which allow for faster data transmission and smaller terminals potentially lowering the cost andcomplexity of equipment. VLEO satellites are expected to be manufacture in high volume and at much lower cost. In this context the activity will investigatethe market potential as well as the required adaptation of current Laser Communication Terminals (LCTs) for accommodation on future VLEO spacecraftincluding potential aero-stable platforms.The activity shall identify technologies that allow to reduce LCT's size, weight, power and cost (SWaP-C) and to accommodate on current or future VLEOspacecraft where gas-surface interactions increase drag forces and aerodynamic pairs, makingtheir operations significantly different compared to satellitesflying in LEO orbits. The assessment of specific materials in contact with the atmosphere in VLEO are aspects of major importance with respect to theirsuitability for demisability and atomic oxygen surface erosion. Finally, requirements from mass manufacturing and design-to-cost constraints are critical toensure adequate development for VLEO constellations.The project's main tasks shall include:- Identify and analyse the VLEO scenarios/systems expected tobenefit from the use of LCTs (ground-satellite links, optical inter-satellite links).- Identify the critical delta-developments oradaptations from existing LCT designs required for operation in VLEO orbits and for links with Earth andbetween spacecraft.- Providean analysis of delta-development covering optomechanical designs, detectors, pointing acquisition and link maintenance, and communicationtransceiver.The use of appropriate materials for demisability and sustained surface erosion from atomic oxygen are to be considered. Design of mass manufacturingis critical.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). title: S3-SW-16 END-TO-END HELIOSPHERIC PREDICTION PART 1
description: This activity will advance physics-based modelling of the solar corona, solar wind, coronal mass ejections (CMEs), and solar energetic particle (SEP) events to improve the prediction of space weather from the Sun to Earth. Using state-of-the-art photospheric magnetic-field observations and in-situ solar-wind measurements as constraints, the activity will enhance the realism and predictive capability of numerical simulations through improved modelling of solar-atmosphere dynamics, solar-wind formation, CME initiation and propagation, and SEP acceleration and transport. The activity will model particle acceleration and release in the lower and middle corona, including flare-associated SEP events and acceleration at CME-driven shocks, together with propagation through evolving coronal and heliospheric magnetic fields. As the first step towards a long-term objective of end-to-end space weather forecasting, the activity will deliver validated software, models, documentation, and demonstrators that significantly strengthen the capability to model and forecast solar drivers of space weather within a common physics-based framework.
